---
title: "Solution: Predictions and Residuals with modelr"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
```

```{r fit-model}
data("diamonds", package = "ggplot2")
mod_loglog <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat), data = diamonds)
```

## Task 1: Create a prediction grid and overlay on scatter

```{r task1}
grid <- diamonds |>
  data_grid(carat = seq_range(carat, n = 200)) |>
  add_predictions(mod_loglog, var = "log_pred") |>
  mutate(pred = exp(log_pred))

ggplot(diamonds, aes(x = carat, y = price)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(data = grid, aes(y = pred), colour = "darkorange", linewidth = 1.3) +
  labs(
    title    = "Diamonds: log-log model fitted curve (price scale)",
    subtitle = "Orange line = exp(fitted log(price)). The curve follows the central trend well.",
    x        = "Carat",
    y        = "Price (USD)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Task 2: Attach residuals and plot vs log(carat)

```{r task2}
diamonds_r <- diamonds |>
  add_residuals(mod_loglog, var = "resid")

ggplot(diamonds_r, aes(x = log(carat), y = resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.07, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_ref_line(h = 0, colour = "darkorange") +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals vs log(carat) — log-log model on diamonds",
    x     = "log(carat)",
    y     = "Residual (log-price scale)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Task 3: Colour residual plot by cut

```{r task3}
ggplot(diamonds_r, aes(x = log(carat), y = resid, colour = cut)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_ref_line(h = 0, colour = "black") +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "RdYlGn") +
  labs(
    title    = "Residuals by cut — remaining structure after log-log model",
    subtitle = "Bands by cut level show that cut explains residual variance.",
    x        = "log(carat)",
    y        = "Residual (log-price scale)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# The residuals DO cluster by cut: Fair diamonds (red/brown) sit mostly
# below zero, while Ideal diamonds (green) sit above zero.
# This means the carat-only model overestimates price for low-quality cuts
# and underestimates for high-quality cuts — cut must be added to the model.
```

## Task 4: Mean residual per cut level

```{r task4}
diamonds_r |>
  group_by(cut) |>
  summarise(
    mean_resid = mean(resid),
    n          = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_resid))

# Ideal cut has the highest mean residual (positive) — meaning the
# carat-only model underestimates their price on average. Ideal-cut diamonds
# command a quality premium that carat weight cannot capture.
# Fair cut has the most negative mean residual — the model overestimates
# their price because carat-only pricing ignores the quality discount.
```
